_doc: Canada zone guides (2026-11-17): Rockies, West Coast, East, Maritimes and Newfoundland. Every thing from Parks Canada, provincial parks, Wikivoyage and Wikipedia (the sources of each zone).

areas.season: Dry and sunny, warm summers (24 °C), cold winters broken by warm chinook winds; the Stampede in the first half of July.
areas.sleep: Downtown or Kensington, by the Bow River.

items.name: Calgary Tower, Stephen Avenue and the Bow River
items.why: The tower's glass floor over the city and the Rockies on the horizon, the pedestrian Stephen Avenue and the river path to Prince's Island.

items.name: The Calgary Stampede
items.book: Rodeo and grandstand seats sell out: buy early
items.why: Ten days of rodeo, chuckwagon races and a fair in early July, the city's great party since 1912.

items.name: Dinosaurs and badlands at Drumheller
items.why: The Royal Tyrrell Museum's dinosaur skeletons, then the hoodoos of the Red Deer badlands, 1.5 h north-east.

items.name: Heritage Park Historical Village
items.why: Canada's largest living history museum: a steam train, a paddlewheeler on the reservoir and a frontier town.

areas.season: Summer days of 22 °C at 1,300 m, snow from November to April; Highway 40 over Highwood Pass is closed 1 December to 15 June.
areas.sleep: Canmore town, 20 minutes from Banff, cheaper and quieter.

items.name: Grassi Lakes
items.why: A short climb past a waterfall to two small turquoise lakes under climbing walls, with old pictographs nearby.

items.name: Ha Ling Peak
items.why: A steep 800 m climb to a summit hanging over Canmore and the Bow Valley.

items.name: Ptarmigan Cirque from Highwood Pass
items.why: From the highest paved pass in Canada (2,206 m) into an alpine bowl with marmots and pikas.

items.name: Rawson Lake above Upper Kananaskis Lake
items.why: Along Upper Kananaskis Lake and up through the forest to a quiet lake under Mount Sarrail's cliffs.

items.name: Kananaskis Nordic Spa
items.why: Outdoor hot pools and saunas in the mountains, open all year, best with snow around.

items.name: Ice walk in Grotto Canyon
items.book: Guided ice walks from Canmore and Banff
items.why: A frozen creek in a narrow canyon, with ice falls and old pictographs, in ice cleats.

items.name: Cross-country skiing at the Canmore Nordic Centre
items.why: The trails of the 1988 Olympic races, lit at night, with ski rentals on site.

areas.season: Summer 22 °C by day and 7 °C at night at 1,380 m; snow from November to April, -15 °C on cold winter days. The ski season runs from November to May.
areas.sleep: Banff town; the Banff Springs for the splurge.

items.name: The Banff Gondola up Sulphur Mountain
items.book: Tickets online; sunset slots go first
items.why: Eight minutes up to 2,281 m and a boardwalk along the ridge over six mountain ranges and the Bow Valley.

items.name: Johnston Canyon
items.why: Catwalks bolted to the canyon wall to the Lower and Upper Falls; in winter the falls freeze and it becomes an ice walk.

items.name: Banff Avenue, Bow Falls and the Banff Springs
items.why: The mountain town's main street, the river falls where Marilyn Monroe filmed, and the castle-hotel of 1888.

items.name: Skiing Sunshine Village
items.why: One of Banff's 'Big 3' ski areas, high on the Continental Divide, often open until late May.

items.name: A cruise on Lake Minnewanka
items.why: The largest lake of the park, a drowned village under the water and bighorn sheep on the road.

items.name: Skiing Mount Norquay
items.why: The small steep ski hill five minutes above the town, the oldest of the 'Big 3'.

items.name: Banff Upper Hot Springs
items.why: A hot pool at 1,585 m facing Mount Rundle, open all year, at its best in the snow.

items.name: Tunnel Mountain Summit
items.why: The small mountain inside the town, a switchback trail to views down both sides of the Bow Valley.

areas.season: Cool even in summer at 1,540-1,750 m (20 °C by day, near 0 at night); the lakes thaw in June and freeze in November. Moraine Lake Road is open about June to mid-October, to shuttles and buses only.
areas.sleep: Lake Louise village, or the Château on the lake.

items.name: Lake Louise and the Lake Agnes Tea House
items.book: The lake's parking fills at dawn: Parks Canada shuttle from the Park and Ride (reserve)
items.why: Along the turquoise lake, then up 400 m past Mirror Lake to a log tea house of 1905 on a hanging lake.

items.name: Moraine Lake and the Valley of the Ten Peaks
items.book: Parks Canada shuttle or a licensed bus, reserved ahead
items.why: The blue lake under ten peaks, seen from the Rockpile; the road is closed to private cars.

items.name: Larch Valley and Sentinel Pass
items.best: Mid to late September, when the larches turn gold
items.why: Up from Moraine Lake through larch meadows to a 2,611 m pass; mid to late September the larches turn gold.

items.name: Peyto Lake and Bow Lake on the Icefields Parkway
items.why: North on the parkway to Bow Lake and the wolf-head lake seen from Bow Summit, the parkway's highest point.

items.name: The lakeshore and the Château at dusk
items.why: The flat path along the turquoise lake under the Victoria Glacier, quiet once the day visitors have gone.

items.name: Skiing the Lake Louise ski resort
items.why: One of the largest ski areas in Canada, facing the Victoria Glacier, open from November to early May.

items.name: Skating on frozen Lake Louise
items.why: A rink cleared on the lake in front of the Château, with ice sculptures in January.

items.name: Marble Canyon and the Paint Pots in Kootenay
items.why: Over the Divide into British Columbia: a narrow limestone gorge and the ochre beds the Ktunaxa used for paint.

areas.season: The British Columbia side of the Divide, a little wetter; the Yoho Valley road to Takakkaw Falls opens about late June to early October, Lake O'Hara's bus mid-June to early October.
areas.sleep: Field village or the Emerald Lake Lodge.

items.name: Emerald Lake
items.why: A green lake under the President Range, a 5 km path around it and red canoes for hire in summer.

items.name: Takakkaw Falls
items.why: One of the highest waterfalls in Canada, 373 m, fed by the Daly Glacier, up a road of tight switchbacks.

items.name: Lake O'Hara
items.book: Bus seat by Parks Canada's spring lottery, or a last-minute release online
items.why: Alpine lakes and ledges walked by few: the park lets only its bus in, seats by lottery.

items.name: The Iceline
items.why: A high path along the moraines under the Emerald Glacier, looking across at Takakkaw Falls.

items.name: Natural Bridge and the Spiral Tunnels
items.why: The Kicking Horse River cutting through rock, and the railway looping inside the mountain to climb the pass.

items.name: Snowshoeing around frozen Emerald Lake
items.why: The lake path under snow, on snowshoes or cross-country skis, with a fire in the lodge after.

areas.season: A valley town at 790 m, warmer than the parks in summer (26 °C); snowy winters, the ski hill from December to April.
areas.sleep: Golden town, or at the foot of the ski hill.

items.name: Skiing Kicking Horse
items.why: One of the biggest vertical drops in Canada, 1,260 m, much of it steep chutes and bowls.

items.name: Kicking Horse gondola and the grizzly refuge
items.why: The gondola to 2,350 m for the view over the Purcells, and the resort's large grizzly refuge on the way.

items.name: Rafting the Kicking Horse River
items.why: Glacier-fed white water through the canyon, one of the best rafting rivers in Canada.

items.name: Golden Skybridge
items.why: Two suspension bridges 130 m above a canyon and its waterfall.

items.name: Cross-country skiing at Dawn Mountain
items.why: Groomed Nordic trails in the forest at the foot of Kicking Horse.

items.name: The timber bridge and the river town
items.why: A railway town on the Columbia and the Kicking Horse, with a timber-frame footbridge built by volunteers.

areas.season: Deep snow in winter (the ski hill gets 10-18 m a year), warm summers in the valley at 450 m; the Meadows in the Sky road to the summit opens about July to September.
areas.sleep: Revelstoke town, on the Columbia River.

items.name: Skiing Revelstoke Mountain Resort
items.why: The longest lift-served vertical in North America, 1,713 m, and deep powder.

items.name: Cat-skiing in the Selkirks
items.why: A snowcat into untracked powder in the mountains around Revelstoke, with a guide.

items.name: Meadows in the Sky
items.why: A road up to the summit of Mount Revelstoke and short walks through alpine flowers, best late July and August.

items.name: Giant Cedars Boardwalk
items.why: A boardwalk in an inland rainforest of 500-year-old western red cedars.

items.name: Rogers Pass and Glacier National Park
items.why: The pass where the railway crossed the Selkirks in 1885, glaciers above and walks along the abandoned rails.

items.name: Revelstoke Railway Museum
items.why: The story of the railway over the Rockies and the Selkirks, with a steam locomotive and a business car.

areas.season: Summer 22 °C in town at 1,060 m, near freezing at the Icefield; winters long and cold. The Maligne Lake cruise runs about June to early October, Edith Cavell road mid-June to mid-October. Part of the town and forest burned in the July 2024 wildfire; check Parks Canada for closed trails.
areas.sleep: Jasper town; cabins along the Athabasca river.

items.name: Maligne Lake and the boat to Spirit Island
items.why: The largest lake of the Rockies, its boat to the islet under the peaks, and moose and bears on the road.

items.name: The Columbia Icefield and the Athabasca Glacier
items.why: Down the Icefields Parkway to the glacier's toe, a ride onto the ice and the glass Skywalk over the Sunwapta valley.

items.name: Mount Edith Cavell and Cavell Meadows
items.why: Under the north face and its Angel Glacier, then up to alpine meadows in flower in July and August.

items.name: Maligne Canyon
items.why: Bridges over a slot canyon 50 m deep; in winter guided walks go down onto the frozen creek between ice falls.

items.name: Mount Robson and Kinney Lake
items.why: An hour west to the highest peak of the Canadian Rockies (3,954 m) and the forest trail to Kinney Lake.

items.name: Miette Hot Springs
items.why: The hottest springs of the Canadian Rockies, in pools at the end of a mountain road.

items.name: Skiing Marmot Basin
items.why: Jasper's ski hill, quiet and uncrowded, from about late November to early May.

items.name: Pyramid Lake at dusk
items.why: A lake and its little island 7 km above the town, under Pyramid Mountain, with elk on the road at dusk.

areas.season: Hot summers in the North Thompson valley; the falls are fullest in May and June. The park road is paved to Helmcken Falls; Clearwater Lake road is gravel beyond.
areas.sleep: Clearwater, at the park's gate.

items.name: Helmcken Falls
items.why: The fourth highest waterfall in Canada, 141 m into a bowl of lava rock; in winter a cone of ice grows below it.

items.name: Dawson, Moul and Spahats falls
items.why: A day of waterfalls on old lava flows; at Moul Falls the path goes behind the curtain of water.

items.name: Trophy Meadows
items.why: Subalpine meadows that are one of BC's great wildflower shows, late July to mid-August.

items.name: Canoe on Clearwater Lake
items.why: A long wild lake at the end of the road, with canoes for hire.

areas.season: Where the prairie meets the mountains, windy; the village is open from May to October and mostly closed in winter. The 2017 Kenow fire burned much of the park; the trails have reopened.
areas.sleep: Waterton Park village on the lake.

items.name: The boat down Upper Waterton Lake
items.why: A cruise into Montana between mountain walls, past the Prince of Wales hotel on its bluff.

items.name: Crypt Lake
items.book: The water taxi to the trailhead
items.why: A boat across the lake, then a climb past waterfalls, a ladder and a tunnel to a hanging lake on the border.

items.name: Bear's Hump
items.why: A short steep climb to the view over the village and the lakes.

items.name: Red Rock Canyon
items.why: A small canyon of red and green rock, and bears and elk on the road in.

areas.season: Canada's hot dry valley, 29 °C in July, warm lake water in July and August; mild winters by the lake, snow at Big White from late November to April.
areas.sleep: Kelowna downtown by the lake, or West Kelowna among the vineyards.

items.name: Okanagan wineries
items.why: Dozens of wineries on the benches over Okanagan Lake, with tastings and lunch among the vines.

items.name: Myra Canyon trestles by bike
items.why: The Kettle Valley Railway's 18 wooden trestles and two tunnels on a cliff above the city.

items.name: Beaches on Okanagan Lake
items.why: City beaches and paddleboards on the warmest big lake in BC.

items.name: Skiing Big White
items.why: Dry 'champagne powder' and a ski-in village, an hour from Kelowna.

areas.season: Mild and wet: dry sunny summers (22 °C), grey rainy winters around 5 °C with snow on the North Shore mountains.
areas.sleep: Downtown, the West End by Stanley Park, or Gastown.

items.name: Stanley Park by the seawall
items.why: Around the park on foot or by bike, past the totem poles of Brockton Point, under the Lions Gate Bridge to the beaches.

items.name: Granville Island and Gastown
items.why: The public market under the bridge, a little ferry across False Creek, and the old town's steam clock.

items.name: Museum of Anthropology at UBC
items.why: Haida poles and the art of the Northwest Coast nations in Arthur Erickson's glass hall.

items.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
items.why: A bridge 70 m over a canyon of rainforest, treetop walkways, and lights in winter.

items.name: The Grouse Grind
items.why: 'Mother Nature's Stairmaster': 853 m straight up the forest to the chalet; the Skyride takes you back down.

items.name: Skiing the North Shore mountains
items.why: Cypress, Grouse and Seymour, twenty minutes from downtown, with night skiing over the city lights.

areas.season: Snow from late November to April in the village (670 m); summers warm, 25 °C, cool on the peaks. The ski season runs about late November to April.
areas.sleep: Whistler Village; Squamish for less.

items.name: Skiing Whistler Mountain
items.why: Half of the largest ski area in North America: the alpine bowls of Whistler, from the village gondola.

items.name: Skiing Blackcomb by the Peak 2 Peak
items.why: Across the Peak 2 Peak gondola to Blackcomb, its glaciers and the long run down the Blackcomb Glacier.

items.name: The Peak 2 Peak gondola and the alpine trails
items.why: Up Whistler, across 4.4 km to Blackcomb 436 m above the valley floor, and walks among alpine lakes.

items.name: Joffre Lakes
items.book: Free BC Parks day-use pass; closed on some days for the Líl̓wat and N'Quatqua
items.why: Three glacier-blue lakes stepping up under the Matier Glacier, north of Pemberton.

items.name: Garibaldi Lake
items.why: Nine kilometres up through the forest to a turquoise lake under glaciers and the Black Tusk.

items.name: Sea to Sky Gondola at Squamish
items.why: Up from Howe Sound to 885 m, a suspension bridge and walks over the fjord, with Shannon Falls at the bottom.

items.name: Scandinave Spa
items.why: Hot pools, saunas and cold plunges in the forest, in silence.

items.name: Audain Art Museum
items.why: BC art from Emily Carr to Haida masks, in a building on stilts in the forest.

areas.season: The mildest city in Canada, dry summers (22 °C) and wet winters near 6 °C; orcas and humpbacks from April to October.
areas.sleep: Around the Inner Harbour or James Bay.

items.name: Inner Harbour, the Parliament and the Royal BC Museum
items.why: Seaplanes and water taxis in front of the Empress and the lit-up Parliament, and the museum of BC's nations and nature.

items.name: Whale watching in the Salish Sea
items.book: Book a day or two ahead in summer
items.why: Orcas, humpbacks and sea lions among the islands, from April to October.

items.name: Butchart Gardens
items.why: A sunken garden in an old quarry, roses in summer, lights in December.

items.name: Dallas Road and Fisherman's Wharf
items.why: The cliff path over the strait with the Olympic Mountains across, ending with fish and chips among the floating homes.

areas.season: Rainforest coast: cool summers (18 °C) with morning fog, very wet winters with Pacific storms from November to February; surf all year in a wetsuit.
areas.sleep: Tofino, or Ucluelet for less.

items.name: Long Beach and the Rainforest Trail
items.why: Sixteen kilometres of surf beach and boardwalks among cedars a thousand years old.

items.name: Hot Springs Cove
items.why: A boat or floatplane up the coast, a boardwalk through the forest, and hot pools in the rocks by the surf.

items.name: Whales and bears by boat
items.why: Grey whales feeding in the sounds from March to October, and black bears turning stones on the shore at low tide.

items.name: A surf lesson at Chesterman or Cox Bay
items.why: Canada's surf town, with schools and wetsuits for hire.

items.name: The Wild Pacific Trail at Ucluelet
items.why: A cliff path past the Amphitrite lighthouse, with storm waves in winter.

items.name: Storm watching
items.why: The winter swells breaking on the rocks, from a beach or the window of a lodge.

areas.season: Mild, wetter in winter; salmon run in late summer and autumn, bear tours from late August to October.
areas.sleep: Campbell River on the strait, or Quadra Island across.

items.name: Grizzly bears in the coastal inlets
items.book: Book weeks ahead: few seats each day
items.why: A boat up the mainland inlets to watch grizzlies catching salmon, late August to mid-October.

items.name: Whales of Discovery Passage
items.why: Humpbacks, orcas and dolphins in the narrow passages between the islands.

items.name: Elk Falls suspension bridge
items.why: A bridge 60 m over the canyon in front of the falls.

items.name: Strathcona Provincial Park
items.why: BC's oldest park, lakes and waterfalls inland and the subalpine Paradise Meadows.

areas.season: A sheltered coast reached only by ferry, sunny summers, mild wet winters.
areas.sleep: Gibsons or Sechelt.

items.name: The Skookumchuck tidal rapids
items.why: A forest walk to narrows where the tide runs at up to 30 km/h in standing waves; go at the peak of the tide table.

items.name: Princess Louisa Inlet and Chatterbox Falls
items.why: A boat through Jervis Inlet into a fjord of granite walls and waterfalls.

items.name: Gibsons harbour
items.why: A fishing harbour with Molly's Reach of the TV series 'The Beachcombers' and the floating homes.

items.name: Kayaking Sechelt Inlet
items.why: Sheltered water and small marine parks, with kayaks for hire in Porpoise Bay.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (27 °C), cold snowy winters around -5 °C; the hockey season runs October to April.
areas.sleep: Downtown, King West or near the Distillery District.

items.name: The CN Tower
items.why: The 553 m tower, its glass floor and the lake from above; the EdgeWalk on the outside for the brave.

items.name: St. Lawrence Market and the Distillery District
items.why: A peameal bacon sandwich in the old market, then Victorian distillery buildings turned into cafés and galleries.

items.name: Royal Ontario Museum
items.why: Dinosaurs, totem poles and world cultures under Libeskind's crystal.

items.name: The Toronto Islands by ferry
items.why: A ten-minute ferry to car-free islands, beaches and the skyline from the water.

items.name: A Maple Leafs game
items.why: Ice hockey in the city of the Hockey Hall of Fame, October to April.

areas.season: Hot summers, mist and ice in winter; the boats run from about April to November, the Winter Festival of Lights from November to January.
areas.sleep: Niagara-on-the-Lake for the town, Niagara Falls for the view.

items.name: The boat into the Horseshoe Falls
items.why: Into the mist at the foot of the falls in a poncho.

items.name: Journey Behind the Falls
items.why: Tunnels through the rock to portals behind the Horseshoe Falls, open all year.

items.name: Niagara-on-the-Lake and the icewine wineries
items.why: A 19th-century town on the lake, the Shaw Festival theatre and the vineyards that make icewine.

items.name: Niagara Glen
items.why: Trails down into the gorge among boulders and old forest, to the river's rapids.

items.name: Winter Festival of Lights
items.why: The falls lit in colour and light displays along the river, November to January.

areas.season: Lakes and maple forest; blackflies in May and June, the maples turn red from late September to early October; snowy winters.
areas.sleep: Lodges and cabins on Highway 60, or Huntsville.

items.name: A canoe day on the lakes
items.why: Paddle and portage between lakes from Canoe Lake, where Tom Thomson painted, looking for loons and moose.

items.name: The Lookout and Track and Tower trails
items.why: Short trails to lookouts over an ocean of maples, red and gold from late September.

items.name: Moose along Highway 60
items.why: Moose come to the roadside pools at dawn and dusk, most in May and June.

items.name: The public wolf howl
items.why: In August, when a pack is near the road, park staff lead the crowd in howling for the wolves to answer.

items.name: Cross-country skiing and snowshoeing
items.why: Groomed ski trails at Fen Lake and Leaf Lake in the snowy winter forest.

areas.season: Hot summers, among the coldest capitals in the world in winter; the Rideau Canal Skateway opens when the ice allows, usually January and February; Winterlude is in February.
areas.sleep: Downtown or the ByWard Market.

items.name: Parliament Hill and the ByWard Market
items.why: The Gothic parliament over the river (the Centre Block is closed for works), the Changing of the Guard in summer, then the market.

items.name: The Museum of History and the National Gallery
items.why: First Nations poles in the Grand Hall across the river, and the gallery under the giant spider Maman.

items.name: Skating the Rideau Canal
items.why: Kilometres of frozen canal through the city, with BeaverTails pastry at the huts, when the ice is thick enough.

items.name: Gatineau Park
items.why: Fifteen minutes from Parliament: lakes, the Champlain Lookout and maple forest red in October.

items.name: Winterlude
items.why: Ice sculptures and snow playgrounds on the first three weekends of February.

areas.season: Ottawa valley weather: hot summers, deep snow from December to March.
areas.sleep: Montebello: the log Château or the village.

items.name: The Parc Omega wildlife drive
items.why: A road through the forest where elk, bison and deer come to the car window, and wolves behind a fence.

items.name: Château Montebello
items.why: Said to be the largest log building in the world (1930), with snowshoeing and skating around it in winter.

items.name: Manoir-Papineau
items.why: The manor of Louis-Joseph Papineau, leader of the 1837 rebellion, on the river.

areas.season: Lake Ontario's outflow, warm summers; the boats run from about May to October.
areas.sleep: Gananoque on the river, or Kingston.

items.name: A cruise through the islands
items.why: Summer houses on rocks just big enough for them, and Boldt Castle on the US side (passport to land).

items.name: Kingston and Fort Henry
items.why: Canada's first capital in limestone, and the fort's sunset ceremony on summer evenings.

items.name: The Thousand Islands Parkway path
items.why: A flat bike path along the river from Gananoque, past the islands.

areas.season: Hot summers full of festivals (Jazz Festival late June to early July), very cold snowy winters with Igloofest in January and February.
areas.sleep: Old Montreal or the Plateau.

items.name: Old Montreal and Notre-Dame Basilica
items.why: Cobbled streets of New France, the blue and gold basilica and the Old Port on the river.

items.name: Mount Royal
items.why: Up Olmsted's park to the Kondiaronk lookout over downtown; skating on Beaver Lake in winter.

items.name: Bagels, smoked meat and Jean-Talon Market
items.why: Wood-fired bagels in Mile End, a smoked meat sandwich, and the farmers' market of Little Italy.

items.name: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts and the underground city
items.why: Canadian and Quebec painting, then the 30 km of tunnels and malls that keep the city warm in winter.

items.name: The Jazz Festival
items.why: Free outdoor concerts across the Quartier des Spectacles, late June to early July.

items.name: Igloofest
items.why: Electronic music outdoors in the Old Port at -20 °C, in snowsuits, January and February.

areas.season: Warm summers, long snowy winters (-12 °C in January); the Winter Carnival runs late January to mid-February, the ice hotel January to March.
areas.sleep: Inside the walls of Old Quebec.

items.name: Old Quebec: Château Frontenac and Petit-Champlain
items.why: The only walled city north of Mexico, the castle-hotel over Dufferin Terrace and the funicular down to the old lower town.

items.name: The Plains of Abraham and the Citadelle
items.why: The 1759 battlefield turned park, and the star fort where the Royal 22e Régiment changes the guard in summer.

items.name: Montmorency Falls
items.why: A waterfall 83 m high, 30 m higher than Niagara, a bridge over it and a cone of ice at its foot in winter.

items.name: Île d'Orléans
items.why: An island of farms across the bridge: strawberries, cider, cheese and old stone churches.

items.name: The Winter Carnival
items.why: Bonhomme's ice palace, night parades, canoe races across the frozen river and snow baths.

items.name: The ice hotel
items.why: Rooms, a chapel and a bar carved from snow and ice, rebuilt every winter, January to March.

items.name: Skiing Mont-Sainte-Anne
items.why: Slopes over the St. Lawrence 40 minutes from the city.

areas.season: Mountains on the St. Lawrence; warm summers, colours in late September and early October, snowy winters with skiing over the river.
areas.sleep: Baie-Saint-Paul, or La Malbaie.

items.name: Hautes-Gorges-de-la-Rivière-Malbaie
items.why: A river between some of the highest rock walls in eastern Canada, by riverboat or canoe.

items.name: L'Acropole-des-Draveurs
items.why: A steep 800 m climb to the summit over the gorges.

items.name: Baie-Saint-Paul and the flavour route
items.why: A village of painters' galleries, then cheese, lamb and cider farms along the river.

items.name: Isle-aux-Coudres by bike
items.why: A free ferry to an island of mills and farms, ridden in a 23 km loop.

items.name: Dog sledding in the Charlevoix forest
items.why: Driving your own team of huskies through snowy forest, with a guide.

items.name: Skiing Le Massif
items.why: The biggest vertical east of the Rockies, with slopes that seem to end in the frozen St. Lawrence.

areas.season: Cool even in summer on the water (5 °C in the boats' wind); whale cruises from about June to October; the village sleeps in winter.
areas.sleep: Tadoussac village on the bay.

items.name: Whale cruise at the mouth of the Saguenay
items.book: Big boats or Zodiacs; book a day ahead in summer
items.why: Minke, fin and humpback whales, sometimes the blue whale, and the white belugas of the St. Lawrence.

items.name: Pointe-de-l'Islet and the dunes
items.why: A short path round the point, where belugas and minkes feed close to the rocks, and the sand dunes beyond.

items.name: The Saguenay fjord and Sainte-Rose-du-Nord
items.why: Up the fjord between cliffs to one of Quebec's prettiest villages.

areas.season: The end of the Gaspé peninsula: cool summers (21 °C), the island's gannets from June to October; little opens from November to May.
areas.sleep: Percé village, facing the rock.

items.name: Bonaventure Island and its gannets
items.why: A boat round Percé Rock to the island, then a walk to one of the largest colonies of northern gannets in the world.

items.name: Percé Rock and the glass platform
items.why: The arched rock in the sea, walked to at low tide, and a glass platform on the cliffs of the geopark.

items.name: Forillon and Land's End
items.why: The tip of the peninsula: seals, whales offshore and a trail to the Cap-Gaspé lighthouse.

areas.season: Mild sea summers (23 °C) and fog, snowy wet winters around -4 °C; hurricane remnants possible from August to October.
areas.sleep: Downtown by the waterfront.

items.name: Peggy's Cove
items.why: A fishing village and its lighthouse on bare granite over the Atlantic; keep off the dark wet rocks.

items.name: The waterfront, the Citadel and Pier 21
items.why: The boardwalk, the star fort over the harbour and its noon gun, and the pier where a million immigrants landed.

items.name: Maritime Museum of the Atlantic
items.why: Titanic's wreckage and the 1917 Halifax Explosion, in the city that buried Titanic's dead.

items.name: Lobster and the Keith's brewery
items.why: Lobster on the waterfront and a pint in Alexander Keith's brewery of 1820.

items.name: Halifax Public Gardens
items.why: A Victorian garden of 1867 with its bandstand and ponds, May to November.

areas.season: The South Shore: mild summers, quiet winters when the museum and many inns close.
areas.sleep: In the old town.

items.name: Old Town Lunenburg
items.why: A UNESCO town of painted wooden houses laid out in 1753, the home port of the schooner Bluenose II.

items.name: Fisheries Museum of the Atlantic
items.why: The fishing schooners on the wharf and the story of the Grand Banks.

items.name: Blue Rocks
items.why: A hamlet of fishing sheds on slate ledges, the best seen by kayak in summer.

items.name: Mahone Bay's three churches
items.why: Three churches side by side on the water, and cafés along the bay.

areas.season: The Fundy side of Nova Scotia; the historic sites and gardens open from about May to October.
areas.sleep: Annapolis Royal's old inns.

items.name: Fort Anne and the town
items.why: Canada's first national historic site, earthworks over the river, and one of the oldest towns in North America.

items.name: Port-Royal Habitation
items.why: A rebuilt French settlement of 1605, among the first in North America.

items.name: Kejimkujik
items.why: Canoe routes of the Mi'kmaq, petroglyphs on the lake shore and a dark sky preserve.

items.name: Whales off Digby Neck
items.why: Humpbacks and finbacks in the Bay of Fundy from Brier Island, June to October.

items.name: Annapolis Royal Historic Gardens
items.why: Gardens through four centuries of the town's history.

areas.season: The highest tides in the world, up to 16 m; cool foggy summers. Hopewell Rocks is open from about mid-May to mid-October.
areas.sleep: Alma village at the park's gate.

items.name: Hopewell Rocks at low and high tide
items.why: Walk on the sea floor between the flowerpot rocks at low tide, then see them islands six hours later.

items.name: Dickson Falls and the coastal trails
items.why: Boardwalks through a mossy gorge to a waterfall, and cliffs over the bay.

items.name: Alma's lobster and the tidal flats
items.why: Boats sitting on the mud at low tide and lobster straight off them.

items.name: Cape Enrage
items.why: A lighthouse on cliffs over the bay, fossils on the beach at low tide.

areas.season: Gentle summers (23 °C) and the warmest sea in Atlantic Canada in August; the Wood Islands ferry runs May to December, the Confederation Bridge all year.
areas.sleep: Charlottetown, or a cottage near Cavendish in summer.

items.name: The red beaches of the national park
items.why: Red cliffs, dunes and warm shallow water at Cavendish and Brackley.

items.name: Green Gables
items.why: The farmhouse that inspired Anne of Green Gables, and the Haunted Wood path.

items.name: Charlottetown, birthplace of Confederation
items.why: Where the 1864 conference planned Canada; red-brick streets, the harbour and Cows ice cream.

items.name: A lobster supper and PEI oysters
items.why: Lobster suppers in church halls and community kitchens, and Malpeque oysters.

items.name: The Confederation Trail by bike
items.why: The old railway across the island, flat among potato fields and harbours.

areas.season: The Highlands: cool summers, fog on the coast, colours in early to mid October; snowy winters with a small ski hill.
areas.sleep: Ingonish, or Cheticamp on the other side.

items.name: Driving the Cabot Trail
items.why: The road around the Highlands, up from the sea onto the plateau and down again; red and gold in early October.

items.name: The Skyline Trail
items.why: A boardwalk to the headland over the Gulf, moose on the way and pilot whales below.

items.name: Whale watching from Pleasant Bay or Cheticamp
items.why: Pilot whales, minkes and dolphins close to the cliffs.

items.name: Franey
items.why: A steep climb to a lookout over Ingonish Bay and the gorge of the Clyburn.

items.name: Middle Head and Ingonish Beach
items.why: A path out along the narrow headland past the Keltic Lodge, between the beach and the open sea.

items.name: Skiing Cape Smokey
items.why: A small ski hill falling to the sea, when the snow is in.

areas.season: Cape Breton's lake country, mild summers; the Celtic Colours festival in October; Louisbourg's full program in summer.
areas.sleep: Baddeck on the lake.

items.name: The Fortress of Louisbourg
items.why: A French fortress town of 1744 rebuilt in full, with soldiers, bakers and fishermen in costume.

items.name: Alexander Graham Bell's Baddeck
items.why: The museum of the telephone's inventor, who summered here and built hydrofoils and kites.

items.name: Sailing the Bras d'Or Lake
items.why: An inland sea of salt water, with bald eagles over the boat.

items.name: A ceilidh and Gaelic music
items.why: Fiddles and step dancing in parish halls, the Gaelic culture brought from Scotland.

areas.season: Cool short summers (20 °C), fog and wind; the Western Brook Pond boat runs about June to October, Gros Morne Mountain is closed until late June. Snowy winters for skiing and snowshoes.
areas.sleep: Rocky Harbour or Norris Point.

items.name: Western Brook Pond
items.why: A 3 km walk over the bog, then a boat into a landlocked fjord between cliffs 600 m high.

items.name: The Tablelands
items.why: Bare orange rock of the Earth's mantle pushed up from the deep, the reason for the UNESCO listing.

items.name: Gros Morne Mountain
items.why: A scree gully to the 806 m plateau with caribou and ptarmigan, and the fjords below.

items.name: Lobster Cove Head at sunset
items.why: The lighthouse over the Gulf at the edge of Rocky Harbour.

items.name: Backcountry skiing and snowshoeing
items.why: The park's ski trails and the Long Range in snow; Marble Mountain's ski hill is near Corner Brook.

areas.season: Foggy, windy and cool: 20 °C in summer, wet snowy winters; icebergs mostly May and June, puffins May to August, humpbacks June to August.
areas.sleep: Downtown, near Water Street.

items.name: Signal Hill and the North Head trail
items.why: Cabot Tower, where Marconi received the first transatlantic radio signal in 1901, and a cliff path down to the Battery.

items.name: Puffins and whales at Witless Bay
items.why: A boat from Bay Bulls to the largest puffin colony in North America, with humpbacks and icebergs in season.

items.name: Cape Spear
items.why: The easternmost point of North America, its 1836 lighthouse and whales offshore in summer.

items.name: Jellybean Row, George Street and a screech-in
items.why: Painted row houses, the street with the most pubs in Canada, and kissing a cod to become an honorary Newfoundlander.

items.name: The Rooms and Quidi Vidi
items.why: The island's museum and gallery over the harbour, then the fishing village and brewery of Quidi Vidi.

items.name: A day on the East Coast Trail
items.why: Cliffs, sea stacks and the Spout, a wave-driven geyser, on a coastal path of 336 km.
